Executed 13 of 18 test cases for Work Schedule creation as the admin (richardtest). API TCs ran via the bearer-replay method (Keycloak JWT captured from the live SPA session, replayed through the BFF /core/api/v1/work-schedules/policies, header x-tenant: eco-flow); UI TCs ran via Playwright MCP. Result: 13 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 PARTIAL / 2 BLOCKED, plus 3 regression candidates not formally run this pass.

The 2 BLOCKED TCs (TC-007 write-only RBAC, TC-008 no-WS-perm RBAC) await a non-admin / role-scoped account — gelosprout2 and gelosprout3 are both admins, so a write-without-publish (or no-permission) account does not exist in the QA Testing entity.

Created artifacts: several QA-WS-TEST-* drafts were left in place (safe — no assignment targets set); 2 published schedules (V2 of QA-WS-TEST-1 and QA E2E Fixed Schedule) were deactivated for cleanup.

Findings / Contract Notes

No product defects were found. The 5 notes below are spec/assumption corrections — the API and UI behave correctly; the test cases need their expectations aligned. Click an affected TC to jump to its details.

#1 API contract

Write endpoints return 201 Created, not 200

Create, duplicate, and edit-as-new-version all return HTTP 201 Created — the TCs assumed 200. The endpoints behave correctly; only the expected-status in the spec is off. Affects the create (POST /work-schedules/policies), duplicate (.../duplicate), and edit-as-new-version (.../edit-as-new-version) paths.

Affected Test Cases

  • TC-002 (primary)
  • TC-010
  • TC-011
  • TC-012
  • TC-013

Recommended correction

Update TC-002 / 010 / 011 / 012 / 013 expected HTTP code to 201.

#2 Payload

blockOrder is 0-based, not 1-based

Day-block blockOrder is 0-based (0..N-1 sequential). The TC payloads sent blockOrder: 1, which the API correctly rejects with a clear HTTP 400. This is a payload-construction error in the TC, not a product fault.

Affected Test Cases

  • TC-002 (primary)
  • TC-010
  • TC-013

Recommended correction

Fix the day-block payload in TC-002 / 010 / 013 to use 0-based blockOrder.

#3 API contract

Wrong-state publish / edit-as-new-version returns 409 Conflict, not 400

Publishing an already-Active schedule, and edit-as-new-version on a Draft or superseded version, both return HTTP 409 Conflict — the TCs assumed 400. The guard fires correctly ("Only Draft schedules may be published"; "Cannot edit a superseded schedule version."); only the expected status differs.

Affected Test Cases

  • TC-006 (primary)
  • TC-014

Recommended correction

Update TC-006 / 014 expected HTTP code to 409.

#4 Routing

Real UI route is /settings/time-tracking-policies

The Work Schedule list/wizard deploys at /settings/time-tracking-policies, not the spec's assumed /time-tracking/work-schedules — consistent with the org-area /settings/{module} pattern. The wizard renders all required fields correctly at the real route.

Affected Test Cases

  • TC-001 (primary)
  • TC-008
  • TC-015

Recommended correction

Update the E2E_WS_URL assumption in TC-001 / 008 / 015 to /settings/time-tracking-policies.

#5 UI flow

Creation is a 4-step wizard; publish is from the list-row menu

The wizard is 4 steps — Scope → Schedule → Assignment → Review. Step 4 offers "Save as Draft" only; there is no in-wizard Publish. Publishing happens from the list via "Policy actions → Publish". The TCs assumed a single-page form with an in-wizard publish.

Affected Test Cases

  • TC-001 (primary)
  • TC-015

Recommended correction

Update the wizard step notes + publish step in TC-001 / 015 (publish via list actions menu).

Blocked Details

TC-007 — RBAC write-only user. No WRITE_ONLY_USER account available; gelosprout2 and gelosprout3 are both admins (provisioned 2026-06-04, not role-scoped). No work_schedules.policies.write-only account exists in the entity. Resolution: provision a non-publish Keycloak role account, or verify RBAC at the permission level in the Keycloak admin console.

TC-008 — RBAC no-access user (UI). No NO_ACCESS_USER account available — same root cause as TC-007.

Environment & Method Notes

1. API auth via bearer-replay. .env.qa has no ApiKey/actor headers, so curl-based API execution is impossible. API TCs ran by capturing the SPA's Keycloak bearer JWT and replaying fetch() through the BFF (/core/api/v1/work-schedules/*). The tenant header is x-tenant: eco-flow (not qa-testing — a key discovery this run).

2. Real module route. Work Schedules deploy at /settings/time-tracking-policies (Note #4).

3. Wizard shape. 4-step wizard — Scope → Schedule → Assignment → Review; Save-as-Draft on step 4; publish via the list-row "Policy actions" menu (Note #5).

4. Cleanup. The two Active schedules created during the run were deactivated; remaining drafts have no assignment targets and were left as-is (safe).

Recommendations

  1. Apply the 5 TC-spec corrections above (201 status, 0-based blockOrder, 409 conflicts, real route, 4-step wizard) — no product changes required.
  2. Provision a write-only and a no-permission role account for the QA Testing entity to unblock TC-007 / TC-008 (RBAC).
  3. Promote the 3 regression candidates (SD-12 atomicity, optimistic concurrency, duplicate lineage) into the regression suite — all behaviours were observed PASS during this pass.
